findings.text: Routine insert_vm_struct is the public entry for adding a prepared area to an address space. It rejects any range that intersects an existing area, requires sufficient accountable memory when the marking known as VMA_ACCOUNT_BIT is present, derives anonymous file and anon offsets from the virtual start address, and on success makes the area visible with an incremented area count. Overlap or resource failure yields an error known as ENOMEM with provisional charges undone.

Purely anonymous areas carry no meaningful file offset until first write fault, yet insertion assigns a stable value to field vm_pgoff derived from field vm_start expressed in pages so that process maps stay consistent and later merge and split handling can reuse file offset logic. A separate anon offset receives the same derived value, and a one time warning is expected if field anon_vma is already set.

Routine vma_link provides all or nothing visibility for a new area. On success the area becomes discoverable through the ordered iterator, its file association is established, the descriptor area count known as map_count is incremented, and the descriptor validates. If iterator reservation fails, nothing is linked and an out of memory error is reported.

Virtual memory exposes integer tunables under the vm group with vector handling and bounds. Entry max_map_count is widely readable and writable with mode 0644 and a zero lower bound. Entry legacy_va_layout appears only with architecture layout support and shares the same mode and lower bound. Randomisation width entries for normal and compat modes appear only with architecture support, use mode 0600, and carry architecture defined minima and maxima.

Boot routine mmap_init establishes counter vm_committed_as at zero with a fatal check on failure, registers the virtual memory sysctl group when sysctl support is enabled, and delegates area cache preparation to area state initialization.

Area state initialization creates a dedicated slab cache named vm_area_struct sized for one descriptor, using an embedded free pointer at field vm_freeptr, a sheaf capacity of 32, and cache properties for hardware line alignment, panic on failure, safe reclamation with read copy update, and accounting.
Tunable sysctl_legacy_va_layout is an integer control selecting legacy virtual address layout behavior, exposed through the virtual memory sysctl table when architecture layout support is present.

User and admin memory reserves are sized from current free memory. Each reserve takes one thirty second of free kilobytes and clamps to a fixed ceiling, using ceiling SZ_128K for the user reserve and ceiling SZ_8K for the admin reserve.

Memory hotplug notifier reserve_mem_notifier maintains reserve tunables across online and offline events and always reports successful handling. On online it refreshes a reserve only when the current value lies below its ceiling, preserving operator increases. On offline it recomputes free memory and refreshes any reserve that now exceeds free memory, emitting an informational message for each reset. Other actions cause no change.

Initialization routine init_reserve_notifier registers the reserve maintainer with the memory hotplug chain at default priority and logs an error if registration fails, while still reporting successful initialization.

Routine mmap_read_lock_maybe_expand selects a locking mode for a possible stack expansion. Read only faults and addresses already inside the area use a read lock and always succeed. A write fault below the start requires the growsdown marking known as VMA_GROWSDOWN_BIT, otherwise it fails without locking. When growth is allowed it takes a write lock, attempts downward expansion, and on success downgrades to a read lock, while failed expansion releases the write lock and reports failure.

Duplication routine dup_mmap serializes source and destination address spaces with write locks. It acquires the source with a killable write lock that can be interrupted, then nests the destination write lock with single depth ordering. Both locks are held for the entire duplication and teardown, with a translation flush for the source before release.

Address space duplication copies total and classified size counters and replicates the ordered store efficiently before per area processing. Areas marked with the dontcopy marking known as VMA_DONTCOPY_BIT are removed from the new store with statistics adjusted and no further copying. Accountable areas validate charging against the source descriptor and any provisional charge is released on failure.

Retained areas require successful cloning of the descriptor with duplicated memory policy and appropriate anonymous handling. Areas with wipe on fork marking known as VMA_WIPEONFORK_BIT show no anonymous linkage in the child and no copied pages, while other areas show forked anonymous linkage with copied page contents. Private huge page information is present in duplicated form when applicable.

File backed areas in the child obtain a new file reference and are inserted into the shared mapping order immediately after the parent entry under the mapping write lock, with writable allowance enabled for shared writable areas and cache maintenance around insertion. The open callback known as open is invoked when present, and architecture plus fork hooks for shared memory and huge page collapsing run only on full success.

Partial duplication failure requires careful teardown. The new store is truncated at the failure point, with zero mapped areas meaning no unmapping, a mid tree failure meaning unmapping up to the failing start, and full write meaning unmapping the entire range. The failing descriptor is hidden from out of memory selection with marking known as MMF_OOM_SKIP and marked unstable with marking known as MMF_UNSTABLE before lock release, with userfault fork state completed on success and failed otherwise.

Routine anon_vma_fork establishes child anonymous linkage. If the parent area has no anonymous structure, it succeeds immediately with no change. Otherwise existing linkage is considered for reuse, and when no reuse occurs the child ends with a new structure showing one active area, child linkage to the parent root, a pinned root reference, assignment as the destination for copy on write pages, and reverse map visibility established under a write lock.

Allocation helper anon_vma_alloc returns a detached anonymous structure with reference count one, zero children and zero active areas, and both parent and root self references. Fork processing later rewrites the root to the parent root.

Routine dup_userfaultfd duplicates userfault handling only when the parent area carries a context and the fork event feature known as UFFD_FEATURE_EVENT_FORK is enabled. Without a context it succeeds with no change, and without the feature it resets the child context and succeeds.

When fork events are enabled, all areas sharing one original userfault context in the parent share one new context in the child through a pending list. The shared new context shows reference count one with copied flags and features, cleared released state, initialized changing lock and counter, grabbed child descriptor, and a corresponding increment of the original changing counter protected by its write lock.

Successful fork completion routine dup_userfaultfd_complete emits one fork event per distinct original userfault context with pending fork records discarded. Each event carries the fork type known as UFFD_EVENT_FORK and the address of the new context in its reserved field, delivered with synchronous completion wait.

Failed fork routine dup_userfaultfd_fail cleans pending userfault fork records without emitting events. Cleaned records show decremented original changing counters with a warning if negative, dropped references on both original and new contexts, and freed record storage, leaving area contexts to later teardown.

Tracing helpers __mmap_lock_do_trace_start_locking and __mmap_lock_do_trace_acquire_returned and __mmap_lock_do_trace_released emit lock lifecycle events. They report start of acquisition, result of acquisition with success indication, and release, each distinguishing read from write mode.

Structure vma_exclude_readers_state coordinates exclusive access to one area. Inputs are the target area pointer known as vma, a sleep state known as state expecting values known as TASK_KILLABLE and TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE, and a detaching flag known as detaching. Outputs are a detached indicator known as detached and an exclusive indicator known as exclusive reporting whether exclusive ownership was achieved.

Per area write exclusion uses a flag added to the area reference count. Acquisition requires the address space write lock, adds the exclude readers flag known as VM_REFCNT_EXCLUDE_READERS_FLAG, and waits interruptibly or uninterruptibly for readers to drain to a target of one for normal use or zero when detaching. Detached areas succeed immediately without waiting. Release subtracts the flag and may observe detachment, with lock dependency tracking acquired and released around the wait.

Routine __vma_start_write establishes write ownership for one area and publishes the current address space sequence number into field vm_lock_seq with ordered store semantics for concurrent lockless readers. If exclusive waiting was needed, it releases the exclusion afterward and expects the area to remain attached, warning otherwise. Interruption during waiting propagates as an error without changing the sequence.

Routine __vma_exclude_readers_for_detach prepares one area for detachment by excluding readers uninterruptibly until the reference count reaches zero with no readers. It assumes write ownership is already held, tolerates transient optimistic readers that decrement promptly, and warns unless the area ends detached.

Routine lock_next_vma performs speculative read copy update lookup of the next area with sequence validation. It begins address space speculation, advances the iterator, and attempts area read locking, retrying from the last address when the area detaches underneath. It verifies that the found area does not end before the search position and, when the start lies ahead, revalidates against concurrent shrinkage or insertion before returning with read ownership.

When speculation fails or validation shows movement, lookup falls back to a read locked search via routine lock_next_vma_under_mmap_lock. The fallback acquires the address space read lock interruptibly, repositions the iterator at the search address, locks the next area for reading, releases the address space lock, and reenters read copy update protection with the iterator positioned after the returned area.

Speculative area iteration can report a retryable error known as EAGAIN when the reference count overflows or the area detaches during acquisition. Callers treat this as a signal to restart from the last search position rather than as a terminal failure, avoiding infinite loops as long as concurrent detachment does not persist indefinitely.

Careful acquisition routine get_mmap_lock_carefully prefers a nonblocking read try lock for the address space. On contention in kernel mode it consults the exception table for the faulting instruction address and fails immediately when no handler exists, otherwise it blocks interruptibly for the read lock.

Upgrade helper mmap_upgrade_trylock is currently unimplemented and always reports failure. Careful upgrade routine upgrade_mmap_lock_carefully therefore releases the read lock first, performs the same kernel mode exception table check as careful acquisition, and then blocks interruptibly for the write lock.

Since optimistic read to write upgrade never succeeds, callers must always handle the upgrade failure path with explicit release and reacquisition, accepting a window where the address space may change between locks.
Compilation unit mmap_lock defines macro CREATE_TRACE_POINTS to enable tracepoint instantiation for its lock events.
